title: Multi-tenant usage aggregation, archive and delivery workflow
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a robust multi-tenant pipeline that aggregates per-tenant usage into daily and hourly CSV payloads, archives older windows, and reliably delivers exports to customer S3 targets and webhook endpoints. Key features: (1) Hourly aggregation consumer that reads event stream (Kafka) and writes partitioned aggregates into Postgres checkpointed state; (2) Export composer that materializes CSVs with canonical header (ts, tenant_id, route, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_usd, request_id) and a signed manifest; (3) Delivery layer supporting direct S3 PutObject with per-tenant prefixes and server-side encryption, and webhook fanout with HMAC payload signing and idempotency keys; (4) Archive TTL and lifecycle: daily exports retained in warm storage 90 days, then moved to Glacier-equivalent archive with immutable manifests; (5) Backfill and reconciliation job to detect missed windows using checkpoints and historical event replay; (6) Failure modes: exponential retry with jitter, configurable DLQ to SQS for manual replay, and automatic fallback to a compressed aggregate for heavy load. SLOs: 99.5% on-time delivery for standard exports within 2 hours of window close, 99.9% integrity (checksum match between manifest and object).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Aggregation job produces hourly CSV for all active tenants for a 24h test window. 2) Delivery pipeline can successfully PUT to a pre-provisioned S3 bucket with server-side encryption and public read disabled. 3) Webhook deliveries include HMAC-SHA256 signature and de-duplication via idempotency token. 4) Backfill driver can detect and repair any missed window within 48 hours and report status to dashboard. 5) Export manifest shows SHA256 and row_count and matches object stored. 6) Unit and integration tests mock failures and DLQ semantics.
implementation_notes: - Use Kafka consumer group 'usage-agg-v2' for parallel aggregation; shard by tenant_id mod N. - Checkpoint writes to Postgres exports.checkpoints (lease, last_event_offset) to guarantee at-least-once with idempotent aggregation upserts. - CSV composer runs in serverless function triggered after window completion; composes compressed gz CSV and writes manifest.json. - S3 delivery uses aws-sdk with retries configured (max attempts 5, base 200ms). - Webhook adapter supports async HTTP 202 semantics, retries with backoff and moves to DLQ after 7 failures. - Use CloudWatch/Prometheus metrics: export_latency_seconds, export_failures_total, dlq_size, checksum_mismatch_total. - Provide migration plan for existing customers with legacy scheduled-CSV: run backfill for last 30 days using a throttled replayer.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Large tenants produce very large CSVs causing memory pressure. Mitigation: stream compose to S3 multipart upload and enforce per-export size limit with chunking and manifest linking. Risk: Missed exports during region failover. Mitigation: active-active consumer groups across regions with lease promotion and cross-region manifest replication. Risk: Data schema drift. Mitigation: Add schema version column in manifest and compatibility checks in composer.
monitoring_and_diagnostics: Dashboards: per-tenant on-time delivery rate, weekly backfill queue length, average export size, checksum mismatch trend. Alerts: >1% tenant failures over 1h, DLQ size growth >100 in 30m, manifest-object mismatch. Provide 'replay' button in Console to trigger backfill for a tenant and a link to the raw export object and manifest in S3.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal canary: enable pipeline for 3 low-volume tenants for 48h. 2) Expand to 50 beta tenants and run backfill for last 7 days. 3) Open to all tenants with feature flag 'export_v2' and monitor SLOs. 4) Turn off legacy exporter after 2 weeks of stable metrics. 5) Post-launch: run large-tenant stress test and finalize archive lifecycle rules.
